summary: The study focuses on the atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD) of molybdenum oxide (MoO3) using (tBuN)2(NMe2)2Mo and ozone, followed by sulﬁdation to form MoS2. The research aims to achieve sub-1 nm nucleation control for large-area monolayer MoS2 synthesis. The process involves optimizing growth conditions, surface treatments, and sulﬁdation temperatures to improve film quality and uniformity. The study highlights the importance of temperature control, precursor exposure, and surface treatments in achieving high-quality, large-area MoS2 films with controlled layer thickness and crystallinity.
evidence: The text describes the use of both thermal ALD and PEALD techniques for depositing MoO3 using (tBuN)2(NMe2)2Mo and ozone, as well as remote O2 plasma. It discusses the optimization of growth conditions, surface treatments, and sulﬁdation temperatures to achieve sub-1 nm nucleation control for large-area monolayer MoS2 synthesis. The study emphasizes the role of temperature, precursor exposure, and surface treatments in achieving high-quality, large-area MoS2 films with controlled layer thickness and crystallinity.
